When a SQL execution error occurs inside a PostgreSQL transaction, you usually need to execute Rollback before you can continue running the next SQL statement.
When this option is enabled, JasonQuery automatically executes Rollback after a SQL execution error, so you can continue running subsequent SQL statements more easily.

When Direct Mode is enabled, JasonQuery connects to the Oracle database directly via TCP/IP without using the Oracle Client.
This mode is suitable when: • Oracle Client is not installed, or you prefer not to rely on it • You want a simpler and more stable way to connect to Oracle
In Direct Mode, only the SID is required. There is no need to configure or verify Oracle Client settings such as tnsnames.ora.
A valid SID is required when Direct Mode is enabled.
Direct Mode provides a connection experience comparable to using the Oracle Client, with a simplified configuration process.

When enabled, JasonQuery will exclude native objects that are shipped with or created by SQL Server, such as system databases (e.g. master, tempdb).
This option helps simplify the object list and focus on user-defined database objects.

When enabled, JasonQuery records important execution information for debugging purposes or for analyzing long-running operations.
This option is not required for normal usage. Enabling it may slightly impact performance.

If enabled, the password will be stored locally in "JasonQuery.db" in encrypted form, and can only be used under the current user account.
If you do not want the password to be stored, please uncheck "Save Password". You will need to enter the password again next time.

This is an advanced option that controls whether connection pooling is enabled.
When enabled, database connections may be kept in a connection pool after being closed, allowing JasonQuery to reuse them without establishing a new physical connection each time.
This improves performance when connections are opened frequently and does not affect query results or transaction behavior.
When disabled, database connections are physically closed each time. A new connection will be established when executing SQL again.
In most cases, it is recommended to keep this option enabled.

When the server and client use different character encodings, SQL execution may fail with encoding errors such as: character with byte sequence 0xe6 0xb8 0xa9 in encoding "UTF8" has no equivalent in encoding "BIG5"
Enabling Unicode allows JasonQuery to communicate with PostgreSQL using Unicode encoding to avoid such issues.

This feature is enabled by default.
When enabled, JasonQuery sets the MySQL client character set to UTF-8 and converts client data according to this character set.
MySQL server version 4.1 or higher is required.

Specifies that the regular expression is compiled to MSIL code, instead of being interpreted. Compiled regular expressions maximize run-time performance at the expense of initialization time.

Enables ECMAScript-compliant behavior for the expression. This value can be used only in conjunction with the IgnoreCase, Multiline, and Compiled values. The use of this value with any other values results in an exception.

Specifies that the only valid captures are explicitly named or numbered groups of the form (?<name>...). This allows unnamed parentheses to act as noncapturing groups without the syntactic clumsiness of the expression (?:...).

Eliminates unescaped white space from the pattern and enables comments marked with #. However, this value does not affect or eliminate white space in character classes, numeric quantifiers, or tokens that mark the beginning of individual regular expression language elements.
Specifies multiline mode. Changes the meaning of ^ and $ so they match at the beginning and end, respectively, of any line, and not just the beginning and end of the entire string.
Specifies that the search will be from right to left instead of from left to right.
Specifies single-line mode. Changes the meaning of the dot (.) so it matches every character (instead of every character except \n).

This feature is enabled by default.
When Paging is enabled and a query completes successfully, pressing "Next Page" will re-execute the previous query to retrieve the next set of rows.
If enabled, the new results will be appended to the existing results. If disabled, only the latest page of results will be displayed.

When this option is enabled, JasonQuery analyzes your SQL input while typing and automatically displays a list of matching members when the conditions are met.
The minimum fragment length controls how many characters are required before Auto Complete is triggered, helping to avoid excessive popups.
The options below allow you to specify which types of members are included in Auto Complete, such as built-in keywords, functions, or user-defined database objects.

Auto Replace allows you to bind frequently used query fragments to short keywords.
After typing a keyword and pressing the space key, JasonQuery automatically expands it into the predefined replacement.
This feature is useful for: • Frequently used query templates • Repetitive SQL structures • Quickly inserting long statements or clauses
You can press Ctrl+Z at any time to undo the replacement.

Insert the ^ symbol in the replacement text. After Auto Replace is applied, the cursor will be positioned at ^, and the symbol will be removed automatically.
This is useful for quickly continuing SQL input after expansion.

When enabled, JasonQuery analyzes the current SQL context while you type and automatically lists available database objects or column members.
For example: • After typing an alias followed by a dot ("."), members of the corresponding table, view, or subquery are listed. • After keywords such as FROM, UPDATE, DELETE, or INSERT INTO, tables or views matching the current input are suggested.
To provide accurate suggestions, JasonQuery may query schema information from the database during SQL editing.

In PostgreSQL, JasonQuery automatically creates a savepoint before executing subqueries required for "Auto List Members".
If a subquery execution fails, for example when the subquery is incomplete or cannot be executed independently, JasonQuery restores the savepoint to prevent affecting the current transaction state.
If the subquery executes successfully, the savepoint is automatically released.
This mechanism applies only to PostgreSQL, as any SQL error in PostgreSQL causes the current transaction to enter a failed state.
This setting affects only helper queries during SQL editing and does not impact user-executed SQL statements.

This option controls how SQL blocks are selected when using Ctrl+Enter.
If enabled, lines containing only whitespace are treated as part of the current SQL block, and JasonQuery continues selecting the full SQL statement.
If disabled, selection stops when a blank line is encountered.

When enabled, JasonQuery executes queries in paging mode, returning a limited number of rows per execution.
After a query completes successfully, you can retrieve the next page of data by clicking the "Next Page" button or by navigating to the last row in the result grid.

[Disconnect immediately after SELECT queries]
After a simple SELECT query is executed, JasonQuery immediately disconnects from the database to avoid holding unnecessary connections.
If there is a pending transaction, JasonQuery keeps the connection open so you can still execute Commit or Rollback.

[Pending transaction warning]
When JasonQuery detects a pending transaction, it shows "Not yet committed or rolled back!" at the bottom of the window, followed by an elapsed-time timer.
JasonQuery shows the first reminder dialog 5 minutes after the pending transaction starts.
If the transaction is still not committed or rolled back after you click OK, JasonQuery will show the reminder again after 5 minutes.

Display column information for Tables and Views in the Query Editor's "Schema Information".
When enabled, JasonQuery retrieves all column names and data types while loading the schema information.
If the database contains a large number of Tables or Views, the schema initialization time may increase significantly.
If you only need to browse object names, disabling this option can improve loading performance.
You can change the setting from [Tools] > [Options] > [Query Editor].

Raw Data Mode significantly improves data display performance.
When enabled, query results are displayed exactly as returned by the database, without much additional formatting or processing.
As a result, the following display-related settings will not be applied: 1. Date formatting 2. Null value style 3. Column type display 4. Column comment display 5. Auto-fit column width 6. Cell Viewer (double-click action)
Note: If the query result contains large text or binary data, this mode may be temporarily disabled for the current query to prevent performance or stability issues.

This setting specifies the maximum time (in seconds) to wait for a server response when executing a query command before generating an error.
The timeout is measured from the moment the query command is sent to the server. It includes only the waiting time for the server response and does not include the time required to fetch data.
This is a connection-level setting and applies to all query editors created using this connection.
The timeout value set in a Query Editor toolbar affects only that editor and takes precedence over this setting.
A value of 0 indicates no time limit.
